text:
sanjay: Heads-up: planning a quick rollout + smoke test for SLO-driven routing + model-variant fallback tomorrow 09:00 PT. Goal: validate p95 latency SLOs and circuit-breaker behavior per customer tier. Need telemetry dashboards, sampling hook, and a safe canary plan.

laura: SGTM. can we define the exact SLOs per tier now so dashboards match?

emily: suggested targets from product: Platinum p95 <= 150ms, Gold p95 <= 250ms, Silver p95 <= 400ms. Availability targets: Platinum 99.95%, Gold 99.9%, Silver 99.5%.

sanjay: thanks. we'll use those. proposal for CB (circuit-breaker) thresholds: open if p95 > +30% over target for 2 consecutive 1m windows OR error rate > 1% for 1m. soft-fallback mode first (route to variant with larger batch/quantized model), hard-fallback (regional reroute) after 3 mins. Thoughts?

mike: prefer to base CB on smoothed signal to avoid noisy opens. maybe use EWMA p95 with alpha=0.3 and require 2 windows of 1m after smoothing. also add request count floor: >200 requests/min per tier to trigger.

nina: telemetry needs: per-tier p50/p95/p99, infra error rate, fallback count, time-to-fallback, trace sample rate, and per-variant latency. I'll add panels. need the metric names we plan to emit.

sanjay: metrics we'll emit in rollout: "redwood.routing.p95_ms", "redwood.routing.errors", "redwood.routing.fallbacks", "redwood.routing.variant.latency_ms" with tags tier, region, model_variant. also emit "redwood.routing.cb_state" (closed/soft_open/hard_open).

laura: can the console show the current CB state per tier and let SREs manually force a soft-open for testing? it'd be handy for smoke tests.

mike: API debate: should we expose a control-plane endpoint to transition CB states or just use feature-flag + audit log? exposing endpoint is convenient but increases surface area.

emily: product wants a one-click rollback/cutover in console for the canary. if we require feature-flag flips + cli we lose that UX. but audit log is required.

nina: compromise: expose control-plane endpoint but locked behind RBAC + internal-only network. all actions emit audit events and traces. canary uses the endpoint via console.

laura: for smoke tests we also need a sampler in the runtime to increase trace sampling for canary requests (only tier=platinum, region=us-west-2), otherwise traces will be too sparse.

sanjay: agree. we'll add header X-Canary-Test:true and runtime will bump trace sampling to 100% for those requests. after 15m canary window we drop to normal.

mike: quick policy snippet for routing operator (rough):
```
policy {
  tiers: [PLATINUM, GOLD, SILVER]
  p95_targets_ms: {PLATINUM:150, GOLD:250, SILVER:400}
  cb_rules {
    soft_open: when ewma(p95,0.3) > target*1.3 && requests_per_min > 200 for 2m
    hard_open: when soft_open persists for 3m OR error_rate > 1% for 1m
    fallback_order: [quantized_variant, regional_variant, burst_pool]
  }
}
```

laura: looks good. can we also track how often fallback_order escalates? that's important for cost forecasting. add metric fallback_escalation_level.

nina: dashboard checklist I'm adding: time-series for p95/p50, stacked bar for fallback breakdown by variant, CB state timeline, per-tier RPS, and a small table with canary traces (trace id, latency, model_variant, region).

emily: for rollout UX: console should show predicted impact: estimated cost delta if fallback quantized_variant used at 5%/25%/100% traffic. that helps PMs approve.

mike: we need a replay harness to run synthetic traffic matching real seq-length distribution to validate p95. can we point to existing perf-sim infra?

sanjay: yes, use perf-sim team job id #rl-sim-72. plan: 15m baseline traffic, enable SLO routing, run 15m canary at 5% traffic to quantify.

laura: smoke test steps (short):
1) create canary flag for tier=platinum, region=us-west-2 at 5%
2) enable increased trace sampling header
3) run perf-sim job rl-sim-72 for 15m
4) watch dashboard panels (p95, errors, fallbacks, cb_state)
5) if soft_open triggers, validate fallback uses quantized_variant and latency behaviour matches prediction
6) if hard_open triggers, stop canary and investigate

nina: I'll wire up alert rules: pager if hard_open for platinum OR if fallback_escalation_level > 1 for >2m. Otherwise post to #eng-oncall slack.

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-config/slo-routing/v1 -> staging (id: deploy-888). Expect ~90s for rollout.

mike: one more API detail: when a request is routed to fallback variant, include header X-Routed-By: slo-routing and X-Fallback-Reasons: [p95_exceed,error_rate] — helpful for logs.

laura: agree, and ensure that logs include original request ID and variant chosen. we'll need that for retro.

sanjay: OK folks — action items: nina adds dashboards + alerts (owner: nina), mike adjusts runtime sampling + headers (owner: mike), laura prepares canary flags + console flow (owner: laura), emily approves cost estimates, sanjay coordinates test window. We'll meet 08:45 PT tomorrow for quick pre-check.

emily: approved on costs for 5% canary.

mike: staging deploy is green. API review passed.

nina: dashboards pushed to staging. linking: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/slo-routing-canary (staging).

laura: canary flag created. UI shows control to abort + audit trail.

sanjay: perfect. see you all at 08:45 PT. I'll post a short reminder 30m before. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout complete: routing-config/slo-routing/v1 -> staging (id: deploy-888) (duration: 1m45s)
